pelage_geometry_and_topology.patch_morphology: Individual patches exhibit irregular, multi-lobed geometries with moderate edge angularity. Patch area is significantly larger on the cervical region compared to the thoracic and flank regions, where they appear more dispersed.
pelage_geometry_and_topology.corridor_network: A continuous network of light-colored interstitial pathways. Junctions are primarily Y-shaped nodes. Pathway thickness is relatively uniform across the visible torso, with slight widening observed at the base of the neck.

dorsal_ridge_profile.edge_serration: The mane along the visible upper neck displays a high-frequency, low-amplitude serrated profile consisting of short, dark-brown filiform structures.

focal_dorsal_anomalies.chronic_feeding_lesions: A distinct, elevated nodular mass is visible on the dorsal ridge at the transition between the neck and shoulder, characterized by a smooth, convex silhouette and textural disruption of the overlying pelage.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: A dark, elongated vertical lesion or scab is visible on the lower posterior flank. Two avian organisms (oxpeckers) are attached to the integument: one at the base of the cranium and one on the posterior flank near the aforementioned lesion.
other_distinctive_markers: Highly prominent localized subcutaneous protrusion on the dorsal-scapular midline.
